paragraphs: The S560 was introduced in 2017 as a V8-powered variant in the W222 S-Class range, replacing the earlier S500 in some markets. It uses the M176 — a 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 that's part of Mercedes' modular V8 family, related to the M177 and M178 used in AMG models. The S560 sat between the six-cylinder diesel and petrol variants and the high-performance AMG models, offering V8 character without the full AMG price or running costs. The M176 in the S560 was available in both rear- and all-wheel-drive (4MATIC) form, and the variant was produced until the W223 generation replaced it in 2020.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every S560 on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre inline-six petrol mild-hybrid engine fitted to the S560 from 2023 to present. The M256 features an integrated starter-generator (ISG) and electric auxiliary compressor, making it a more modern and efficient design than the older M276 V6. We replace timing chains, bearings, water pump and gaskets as standard on every M256 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: The S560 uses one engine across its entire production run: the M176. However, variations exist — 4MATIC (all-wheel-drive) models have different ancillaries and engine mounts, and there were various power output levels across different markets.
